@graph.name: Box Palletizer
@graph.description: A box palletizer is a robotic system that picks corrugated boxes from a conveyor and stacks them onto pallets in programmed layers, with patterns and grippers matched to each box size. TRF Industrial Automation builds box palletizers on TRFCobot, TRFCompact and TRFSpeed, or as a custom palletizer, and the right model is defined by your line setup and speed.

mainEntity.name: Can One Box Palletizer Handle Different Box Sizes and Pallet Patterns?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, within the validated application. TRF palletizing platforms run multiple recipes and pallet patterns, so one palletizer can handle several box sizes, and the operator selects the recipe at changeover. The practical limits are physical: the tool must hold the smallest and the largest box, the robot must reach the farthest corner of the top layer, and the layout sets the number of pallet positions.

mainEntity.name: How Many Boxes per Minute Can a Robotic Palletizer Handle?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the platform. TRFCobot covers about 1 to 10 cases per minute, TRFCompact about 5 to 15 and TRFSpeed about 10 to 35, as typical ranges for commercial screening. For a box operation, size the palletizer for the peak rate, add accumulation to absorb waves, and let TRF confirm the final rate with your boxes, tool, pattern and reach.

mainEntity.name: Can a Box Palletizer Fit a Distribution Center With Limited Floor Space?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often, yes. TRFCobot has a small footprint for areas where a traditional robotic cell is hard to install, and TRFCompact brings an industrial robot into a compact, standardized cell for existing buildings. The final layout depends on the number of pallet positions, forklift access to full pallets and the conveyor routing, all confirmed for your building.

mainEntity.name: Can a Box Palletizer Keep Labels Facing Out?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, when the recipe defines box orientation and boxes reach the robot in a known orientation. Labels and barcodes facing out let pallets be scanned without breaking them down. The robot can rotate a box during the move, and barcode or vision interfaces on TRFIntraflow conveyors can identify each box before the pick. Label-out patterns are validated with your actual label positions.

mainEntity.name: How Much Does a Box Palletizer Cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cost depends on the platform, peak rate, heaviest box, end-of-arm tool, number of pallet positions, pallet handling and conveyor integration. As a reference, list prices are US$ 120,000 for the TRFCobot Dual, US$ 180,000 for the TRFCompact Dual and US$ 350,000 for the TRFSpeed 100, EX Works Lenexa, Kansas, installation not included. The robotic palletizer cost page explains each factor.

mainEntity.name: What Is the Typical Payback Period for a Robotic Palletizer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Payback depends on the labor hours the palletizer replaces, shifts per day, local labor cost and the installed cost of the system. For box operations, count the people who stack boxes on every shift today. The palletizing ROI calculator applies this method to your location, your shifts and the people who palletize by hand today, and a TRF Sales Engineer completes the estimate with your project costs.

mainEntity.name: What Information Should I Prepare to Size a Box Palletizer?

acceptedAnswer.text: List every box size the palletizer must handle, with dimensions and weight range, the box top and label positions, boxes per minute at peak per line, shifts per day, box changes per shift, required pallet patterns and maximum height, and a drawing of the floor space. Add the systems the palletizer must talk to, such as the case sealer, sorter, wrapper and warehouse system.
